### The Centrality of Passover
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/centrality-passover
Passage: Numbers 9:13
Points:
- Observing the Passover was vital for every covenant member to remember God's redemption from Egypt.
- God provided a gracious postponement for those who were ceremonially unclean or traveling, ensuring they were not excluded.
- Willful failure to observe the feast carried the severe judgment of being cut off from God's people.
- The command underscores the solemn priority believers today must place on participating in the Lord's Supper.
- Taking the new covenant sacrament in faith nourishes union with Christ and unity within the church.

### Read the Bible: Numbers 9, Psalm 45, Song of Songs 7, Hebrews 7
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/numbers-9-psalm-45-song-of-songs-7-hebrews-7/
Passage: Numbers 9:1-14
Points:
- Celebrating the first anniversary of Passover created a crisis for men defiled by contact with a dead body.
- Rather than improvising an answer, Moses consulted the Lord to receive divine guidance.
- God allowed ceremonially defiled people to observe the feast one month later, while barring postponements made for mere convenience.
- This episode shows that biblical laws function within a hierarchy of importance rather than rigid legalism.
- Understanding how these covenant laws fit together reveals how they ultimately point to Christ.

### Bible Pathways 02/16/2003
Author: Bible Pathways Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-02-or-16-or-2003-1184778.html
Passage: Numbers 9:1-3
Points:
- Israel's observance of the second Passover served as a necessary memorial of their deliverance from bondage.
- Redemption meant Israel was freed from Egyptian slavery specifically to obey and follow the Lord.
- Failing to present the Lord's appointed offering resulted in separation from the community.
- The Passover lamb pointed forward to Christ, who was sacrificed to free believers from sin.
- Partaking of the Lord's Supper prepares and strengthens Christians for their ongoing journey through life.
